correctness.rationale: The proof derives exact Smith valuations (0,1) for A-I, (1,1) for A^2-I, and (j,j+1) for A^(2^j)-I with j>=2 using determinant valuation nu_2(1+u^2)=1 and unimodular doubling. Kernel sizes and period inversion give all counts, including boundary moduli 2 and 4. The 54 exact matrix checks and 42 complete state-space checks agree; they do not replace the proof.

evidence: Fiebig–Mbirika–Spilker §3.2 cites Wall (1960), Corollary to Theorem 8, for a criterion when an arbitrary-seed Fibonacci sequence has the same period as the canonical Fibonacci sequence. This does not supply cycle multiplicities for K congruent to 2 modulo four.

A published matrix-dynamics result titled “Exact powers-of-two torus orders for all-to-all coupled cat maps” studies a different coupled cat-map family and reports permutation orders rather than these counts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general finite-module Smith-kernel theorem could in principle imply this special family, but such generic machinery without the explicit valuations and all-cycle distribution is not the same stated classification. No inspected broader result gives the requisite numerical parameters for this 2-adic family; unindexed wider theorems remain a risk.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons with the natural 2024 primary literature and targeted equivalent-claim, broader-theorem, and exact-table searches identify no statement of the complete all-seed cycle multiplicities for K congruent to 2 mod 4. Standard-seed periods and equality of two distinguished periods do not imply all fixed-point counts. Risk remains from unindexed general matrix dynamics.
residual_risks: The original full text of Wall (1960) was not accessible; its cited scope is coefficient-one Fibonacci rather than this even-K family.
A preexisting unindexed general Smith-normal-form analysis of all recurrence states over 2-power rings may imply the exact formulas.
No negative originality conclusion is drawn from search absence alone.

value.rationale: This is a motivated natural complete classification of the finite-state trajectories of all K-Fibonacci recurrences over 2-power rings for an infinite coefficient congruence class. It strengthens known period-only statements to exact distribution of every primitive orbit and proves an invariant census independent of K/2. No arbitrary finite threshold or external downstream claim is needed.
